lines.text: What would happen to you if lightning struck the swimming pool while you were taking a dip?
A typical lightning bolt carries over thirty thousand amperes and three hundred million volts of raw energy.
While pure distilled water is an insulator, swimming pool water is packed with conductive chlorine salts and minerals.
When lightning hits, the electrical current spreads out horizontally across the water's surface.
Anyone with their head or shoulders above water becomes the path of least resistance.
The shock causes immediate cardiac arrest, severe internal burns, and instant loss of consciousness.
That is why lifeguards order everyone out of the pool the instant thunder rumbles.
